title: The Wise Kitchen
about: Every recipe and kitchen note here comes from the Food/Recipes folder in Jonathan's bookmarks, gathered in November 2026: 91 recipes and 8 reference guides.

Each recipe has been rewritten into the same layout, with ingredients, numbered steps and a few tips, and the original source just under the title. Blog stories and photos are left out, so visit the source if you want them.

Quantities are as the original gave them (US cups and spoons, plus grams where the source used them). Temperatures are in °F with °C alongside. A few recipes come from YouTube videos; for those, the ingredients and steps were taken from the video and its description.

Only two bookmarks didn't make it in: Perfectly Crispy Bacon, a short Imgur clip that couldn't be opened while the book was being made; and Shaping Into A Pie, a pizza-dough shaping video that went offline when YouTube closed the channel that posted it.

chapters.title: Poultry
chapters.blurb: Roast chicken and game hens, two kinds of stuffed chicken breast, three ways with duck, easy weeknight bakes and a couple of takeout favorites made at home.

items.title: Air Fryer Chicken Tenders
items.time: Prep 5 min · Cook 30 min in batches

steps.text: Season the chicken with the salt and some pepper.
Put the eggs in one shallow bowl and mix the breadcrumbs and panko in another.
Dip each tender in egg, then in the crumbs, shaking off the excess. Spray both sides generously with oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F (200°C).
Cook in batches, 5–6 minutes per side, until golden, crisp and cooked through. Serve with lemon wedges.

tips: Use gluten-free breadcrumbs and panko for a gluten-free version.

items.title: Avocado Smothered Chicken

items: 2 lb thin-cut boneless, skinless chicken breasts
¼ cup oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, diced

ingredients.title: Sweet chili drizzle (or use store-bought sweet chili sauce)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Lay the chicken flat in a large baking dish and season with half the salt and all the pepper.
Mash the avocados with the sun-dried tomatoes, red onion, cilantro and the rest of the salt, leaving some chunks.
Spread the avocado mixture over each piece of chicken and top with the cheese.
Cover with foil and bake 25–35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F / 74°C). For browned cheese, uncover and broil for the last 3–5 minutes.
Whisk the drizzle ingredients together, using 1 tbsp chili sauce for mild or 2 for spicy.
Serve over rice or sautéed spinach, drizzled with the sauce.

tips: To freeze, assemble through step 3, wrap the dish well and freeze unbaked. Thaw completely before baking.
Avocado browns in the fridge, so freeze leftovers rather than refrigerating them.

items.title: Baked Salsa Chicken

items: 2 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts, halved horizontally into thin cutlets

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a baking dish.
Rub the chicken all over with the taco seasoning, lay it in the dish and spoon the salsa over the top.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes, until cooked through (165°F / 74°C).
Scatter over the cheese and bake 2–3 minutes more, until melted. Sprinkle with cilantro.

tips: The Homemade Taco Seasoning in the Sauces chapter works well here.

ingredients.title: Marinade
items: 1 can (7 oz) chipotle peppers in adobo: 4 of the peppers plus all of the sauce

steps.text: Put all the marinade ingredients in a blender, using just 4 chipotles and all the adobo sauce (keep the leftover peppers for another use). Blend on low to medium for 1–2 minutes, until smooth.
Put the chicken in a gallon zip-top bag, pour in the marinade, press out as much air as possible and seal. Refrigerate overnight, or at least 8 hours.
Heat a cast-iron skillet (or grill) over medium to medium-high heat. Add the chicken and sprinkle the tops with kosher salt.
Cook 4–5 minutes, until deeply charred underneath, then flip and cook about 3 minutes more, until 165°F (74°C) inside. Pulling it at 163°F lets carryover heat finish the job.
Slice each thigh lengthwise into strips, then cut across into ¾-inch cubes, just like the restaurant does.

items.title: Cornish Game Hens with Garlic and Rosemary

steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Rub the hens with 1 tbsp of the oil and season lightly. Put a lemon quarter and a rosemary sprig in each cavity. Set the hens in a large, heavy roasting pan and scatter the garlic around them.
Roast 25 minutes. Meanwhile, whisk the wine, broth and remaining 2 tbsp oil together.
Turn the oven down to 350°F (175°C). Pour the wine mixture over the hens and roast about 25 minutes more, basting every 10 minutes, until golden and 165°F (74°C) near the bone.
Move the hens to a platter, tipping the juices from the cavities back into the pan. Discard the lemon and rosemary and tent the hens with foil.
Pour the pan juices and garlic into a saucepan and boil about 6 minutes, until reduced to a sauce.
Spoon the sauce and roasted garlic over the hens and garnish with the remaining rosemary.

tips: The author serves these with crusty garlic bread and a light Chianti.

items.title: Garlic Herb Butter Roast Chicken

ingredients.title: Chicken
items: 1 whole chicken, about 4 lb (1.8 kg), at room temperature, giblets removed

ingredients.title: Pan gravy (optional)
items: 2 tbsp chicken fat skimmed from the drippings

steps.text: Heat the oven to 430°F (220°C), or 400°F (200°C) on fan. Line a baking tray with foil or grease a roasting pan.
Trim any excess fat from the chicken and pat it completely dry.

Drizzle the oil, melted butter, wine and the juice of half the lemon over the bird, working some under the skin and into the cavity. Season generously inside and out with salt and pepper, then scatter over the parsley.
Rub the minced garlic all over the skin.
Fill the cavity with the halved garlic head, the rosemary and the squeezed lemon half. Tie the legs together.
Roast breast-side up for 1 hr 15–20 min, basting once halfway, until the juices from the thigh run clear (165°F / 74°C in the thickest part).
Baste again, then broil for 2–3 minutes to finish browning the skin.
Tent with foil and rest 10 minutes. Serve with the pan juices and the remaining lemon half cut into wedges.
Pour the pan juices into a jug or fat separator and let the fat rise for a minute.
Spoon 2 tbsp of the fat into a small saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth, then the rest of the dark pan juices.
Simmer 2–3 minutes, stirring, until it coats a spoon. Season to taste.

tips: Not enough fat for the gravy? Make up the difference with melted butter. If it gets too thick, loosen it with a splash of broth.
Leftover meat, off the bone, keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

items.title: Herb-Brined Cornish Game Hens
items.time: Prep 35 min, plus 1–2 hr brining · Roast 35–40 min

ingredients.title: Brine
items: 1 quart water, plus 1½ quarts cold water

ingredients.title: Herb butter
items: 3 tbsp plus 1 tsp olive oil, divided
⅓ cup packed fresh parsley sprigs

ingredients.title: Vegetables
items: 2 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
2 small red onions, cut into wedges

steps.text: **Brine:** Boil the salt, brown sugar, 12 peppercorns, herbs, garlic and 1 quart water, stirring until dissolved. Off the heat, add the 1½ quarts cold water and let cool.

Nest one roasting bag inside the other, add the hens and the cooled brine, press out the air and seal. Set in a roasting pan and refrigerate 1–2 hours, turning occasionally. Drain and pat the hens dry.
**Herb butter:** Pulse the 14 peppercorns and 2 garlic cloves in a food processor until coarsely chopped. Add the butter, 3 tbsp oil and the herbs and process until smooth.
Loosen the skin on each hen and spread half the herb butter underneath. Pin the skin under the breast with toothpicks, tie the legs and rub the rest of the butter on top.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). In a 15 × 10 × 1-inch pan, toss the Brussels sprouts and onions with the remaining 1 tsp oil, ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper and spread them out.
Set the hens breast-side up on the vegetables. Roast 35–40 minutes, until a thermometer in the breast reads 165°F (74°C). If they brown too fast, tent loosely with foil.
Rest the hens under foil for 10 minutes, then carve and serve with the vegetables.

items.title: Killer Chicken Thighs
items.time: Prep 15 min, plus marinating · Bake 30 min

items: ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Mix everything except the chicken in a large bowl or zip-top bag. Add the thighs and turn to coat. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes to 2 hours, or ideally overnight.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Put the chicken, skin-side up, in a baking dish with all the marinade. Bake uncovered 25–30 minutes, until 165°F (74°C) inside, basting with the pan juices after 15–20 minutes.
For crisper skin, broil for the last 2–3 minutes. Watch closely, since the sugars burn quickly.

items.title: Mushroom, Broccoli, and Cheese Stuffed Chicken

source.name: Allrecipes · recipe by Soup Loving Nicole

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with foil.
Microwave the broccoli with 2 tbsp water on High for 2 minutes, then drain.
In a large bowl, mix the broccoli with the pepper Jack, mayonnaise, mushrooms and garlic powder.

Season the chicken on both sides with paprika, salt and pepper. Cut a deep pocket into the side of each breast without cutting all the way through, fill with the broccoli mixture and set on the baking sheet.
Bake about 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) in the center.

items.title: Oven-Baked Chicken and Rice

ingredients.title: Chicken
items: 6 skinless chicken thighs, bone-in or boneless

ingredients.title: Garlic mushrooms (optional)
items: ¼ cup chopped chives or green onions, divided
¼ tsp each salt and pepper

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a shallow bowl, mix the oil, brown sugar, oregano, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, salt and pepper. Turn the chicken in it until evenly coated. (If you have time, marinate overnight.)
Grease a 10 × 15-inch baking dish. Add the onion, garlic, oil, salt, pepper, hot broth, hot water and butter, and stir until the butter melts. Stir in the rice.

Lay the chicken over the middle of the rice. Cover tightly with foil and bake 30 minutes. Uncover, spray the chicken with oil and bake another 25–30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the rice is tender. Broil 3–5 minutes to brown the top.
Lift off the chicken, stir the rice, return the chicken, then cover and rest 10 minutes; the rice finishes steaming as it sits.
**Mushrooms (optional, while it rests):** Melt the butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic 30 seconds, add the mushrooms and cook until soft. Stir in 2 tbsp of the chives and season.
Fluff the rice and fold in the mushrooms. Return the chicken, sprinkle with the rest of the chives and the parsley, and serve.

tips: Use skinless thighs. Skin-on thighs leave the rice gluey and undercooked.
Bone-in breasts or drumsticks work in the same time.
Stick to long-grain, basmati or jasmine rice. Short-grain, risotto and instant rice won't cook right.
Center the chicken so all the rice sits under liquid and cooks evenly.

steps.text: Stir the pineapple, stock, brown sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, garlic powder and pepper together until the sugar dissolves. Put the chicken in the pressure cooker and stir in the sauce to coat.
Lock the lid and bring up to High pressure (on a stovetop cooker, lower the heat once it reaches pressure). Cook 20 minutes.
Mix the cornstarch with the cold water.
Quick-release the pressure. Lift the chicken onto a serving dish with a slotted spoon and cover with foil.
Whisk the cornstarch mixture into the sauce, bring it to a boil (use Sauté on an electric cooker) and cook about 3 minutes, stirring often, until thickened. Spoon over the chicken.

items.title: Stuffed Chicken Parmesan
items.note: Chicken Parmesan with a pocket of mozzarella in the middle: breaded, pan-fried until golden, then baked in tomato sauce.

steps.text: Season the chicken with salt. Cut a deep pocket into the side of each breast without cutting all the way through.
Fill the pockets evenly with the mozzarella, then press the edges together to seal.

Set out the flour, beaten eggs and bread crumbs in three shallow bowls. Dredge each breast in flour and shake off the excess, keeping the pocket closed. Dip it in the egg, then coat it evenly with bread crumbs.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and fry the chicken until golden brown on both sides.
Spread two-thirds of the tomato sauce over the bottom of a baking dish and set the chicken on top. Cover with the rest of the sauce and sprinkle with the Parmesan and basil.
Bake for 20 minutes.

tips: This was bookmarked as a Gfycat clip of Tasty's video. Gfycat has since shut down, so the recipe here comes from Tasty's own site.
Large breasts may need longer in the oven. The chicken is safe once the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C).

ingredients.title: Glaze
items: ⅓ cup packed dark brown sugar

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed baking sheet with heavy-duty foil and grease it.
Whisk the glaze ingredients together in a small bowl.
Cook the onion in the olive oil over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cook 1–2 minutes more without browning. Let cool.

In a large bowl, whisk the salt, pepper, paprika, thyme, Worcestershire, Dijon, eggs and ¼ cup of the glaze. Add the cooled onion, the turkey and the breadcrumbs and mix with your hands until evenly combined.
Divide the mixture in half and shape each portion on the baking sheet into a loaf about 6 inches long, 4 inches wide and 1½ inches high.
Spread the remaining glaze over the loaves, letting it run down the sides.
Bake about 45 minutes, until cooked through (165°F / 74°C in the center). Scrape away any fat, slice and garnish with parsley.

ingredients.title: Duck and stuffing
items: 1 whole duck (about 5 lb), neck and giblets saved
1 can (6 oz) frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed, divided
1 apple, peeled, cored and cut into chunks

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Rinse the duck, trim the excess fat from around the cavity and prick the skin all over with a fork, without piercing the meat.
Rub 1 tbsp of the orange juice concentrate over the skin and inside the cavity, then rub in the minced garlic and season inside and out with salt and pepper.

Mix about 2 tbsp of the chopped onion with the raisins and apple and stuff the cavity loosely. Truss the duck and set it on a rack in a roasting pan. Scatter the rest of that onion and the carrot slices around it.
**Basting mixture:** Whisk the remaining orange juice concentrate with the ½ cup broth, ¼ cup lemon juice, salt and pepper.

Roast 1 hour, basting now and then. Pour off the rendered fat, then roast about 1 hour more, still basting, until the thigh reads 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear. Save any leftover basting mixture.

**Duck stock (while the duck roasts):** Brown the neck and giblets in the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic and carrot and cook about 5 minutes, until the onion is translucent. Add the broth, lemon juice, orange juice, parsley, salt and pepper, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 1 hour. Strain and set aside.
Move the duck to a warm platter with the roasted vegetables, spoon the stuffing into a bowl and let the duck rest about 15 minutes.

**Sauce:** Skim the fat from the roasting pan, add the leftover basting mixture and scrape up the browned bits over medium heat. Add the duck stock, bring to a boil and reduce by about half, stirring, about 10 minutes. Whisk in the sour cream until glossy and pour over the carved duck.

items.title: Peking Duck
items.time: Prep 15 min, plus 2 hr to overnight marinating · Cook 1 hr 35 min

steps.text: Rinse the duck inside and out, pat dry and cut off the tail.
Mix the cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, white pepper and cloves. Sprinkle 1 tsp of the mix inside the cavity.
Stir 1 tbsp of the soy sauce into the rest of the spice mix and rub it all over the outside of the duck. Halve 1 green onion and tuck it into the cavity.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Set the duck breast-side up on a rack in a wok or large pot over simmering water and steam 1 hour, topping up the water as it evaporates.
Lift the duck out, letting the juices and green onion drain from the cavity.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Put the duck breast-side up in a roasting pan, prick the skin all over with a fork and roast 30 minutes.
Mix the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce with the honey and brush it over the duck. Turn the oven up to 500°F (260°C) and roast about 5 minutes, until the skin is deep brown but not charred.
**Plum sauce:** Stir together the plum jam, chutney, sugar and vinegar. Chop the remaining green onions.
Serve the whole duck on a platter with the orange slices and parsley, with the plum sauce and green onions alongside.

items: 3 cups peeled, cored and chopped apple

steps.text: Rinse and dry the duck, then rub it inside and out with salt, pepper and the poultry seasoning.

Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and celery until tender. Mix with the apple and cornbread crumbs in a bowl to make the dressing, adding a splash of water if it seems dry.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Stuff the duck with the dressing and sew the opening closed with kitchen twine. Rub the skin lightly with the olive oil and set the duck in a shallow roasting pan or 9 × 13 dish.
Roast 60–80 minutes, until the thickest part reads 180°F (80°C).

chapters.title: Beef & Lamb
chapters.blurb: A pan-seared rib-eye, a reverse-seared steak and a grilled Santa Maria tri-tip, Mississippi pot roast, Swedish meatballs and lomo saltado, plus braised lamb shanks and a slow-roasted rabbit.

items.title: Chef John's Swedish Meatballs
items.time: Prep 30 min, plus 1 hr chilling · Cook 45 min

source.name: Allrecipes · recipe by John Mitzewich (Chef John)

ingredients.title: Meatballs
items: ¾ tsp freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: **Meatballs:** Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion with the salt about 6 minutes, until translucent.
Tip the onion into a large bowl and stir in the eggs, breadcrumbs, milk, pepper, nutmeg, allspice and cayenne. Mix in the beef and pork until evenly combined. Cover and refrigerate 1 hour.

**Gravy:** Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook 4–5 minutes, until golden. Slowly whisk in the broth. Raise the heat to medium-high, whisk in the cream and bring to a simmer. Stir in the sugar and Worcestershire and simmer 6–7 minutes, until slightly thickened. Season and set aside off the heat.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with foil and coat it lightly with cooking spray.
With wet hands, roll the mixture into balls of 2–3 tbsp each and set them on the sheet.
Bake about 20 minutes, until browned and 160°F (71°C) in the center.
Add the meatballs to the gravy and warm through over medium-low heat, about 5 minutes.

items.title: Grilled Santa Maria Tri-Tip
items.time: 40 min, plus at least 1 hr in the rub

source.name: NYT Cooking · recipe by Kim Severson

items.note: Tri-tip is the boomerang-shaped roast at the heart of Santa Maria barbecue. You may have to ask a butcher or the store's meat counter to order one. Two pounds is a good size, but grab a bigger one if you see it; leftovers make excellent sandwiches.

items: 3 tbsp beef rub of your choice

steps.text: Trim off the silver skin. If there's a thick layer of fat, slice some of it away, but leave plenty to baste the meat as it cooks.
Before seasoning, look at which way the long muscle fibers run on each end of the roast. The grain changes direction partway along, and you'll want to know where when it's time to carve.
Sprinkle the rub all over the meat and massage it in lightly. Cover and refrigerate for at least an hour, or as long as overnight. Take it out of the fridge an hour before cooking.
Build a charcoal fire or heat a gas grill to high. Sear the roast until the first side is well browned, 6–8 minutes, watching for flare-ups. Turn it and sear the other side for about as long.

Turn the gas down to medium-high, or move the roast to a cooler part of the charcoal grill. Turn it again and cook 8–10 minutes, then flip and keep cooking. A 2-lb roast takes about 20–25 minutes in all. It's ready when an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads 130°F (54°C).
Rest the roast on a cutting board for 10–20 minutes. Cut it in two at the bend, where the grain changes direction, then slice each piece thinly against the grain.

tips: Any beef rub works here. Traditional Santa Maria seasoning keeps it simple: mostly salt, pepper and garlic.

items.title: Mississippi Pot Roast

items: 1 packet dry onion soup mix (or au jus gravy mix)

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat (or use your slow cooker's sear setting).
Pat the roast dry, season both sides with salt and pepper, and sear 2–3 minutes per side.
Move it to the slow cooker. Sprinkle the ranch mix and onion soup mix over the top, set the butter on the roast and tuck the pepperoncini on and around it.
Cover and cook on Low for 8 hours, without lifting the lid.
Shred the meat with two forks, discard any large fatty pieces, and serve with the juices.

tips: Don't cook it on High; it needs the long, low cook.
Every time the lid comes off you lose heat and moisture, so leave it closed.

items.title: Pan-Seared Rib-Eye

steps.text: Put a 10–12-inch cast-iron skillet in the oven and heat it to 500°F (260°C). Let the steak come to room temperature while it heats.
When the oven is hot, move the skillet to the stovetop over high heat for 5 minutes. Lightly oil the steak and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Lay the steak in the center of the dry, very hot skillet and leave it alone for 30 seconds. Flip and sear 30 seconds more.
Move the pan to the oven for 2 minutes, flip the steak, and give it 2 minutes more for medium-rare. For medium, add 1 minute to each side.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 2 minutes. Serve whole or thinly sliced.

tips: The skillet handle stays dangerously hot after it comes out of the oven, so keep a mitt on it.
Expect smoke. Turn on the vent fan before the steak goes in.

items: 1 lb (455 g) sirloin steak, cut into strips
1 lb (455 g) french fries, cooked and hot

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the steak, season with salt and pepper and sear until browned, 5–6 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the onion to the pan and cook about 5 minutes, until soft and browned.
Add the tomato, garlic and ají amarillo paste and cook 5–7 minutes, until the tomato has released some juice but still holds its shape.
Stir in the soy sauce and vinegar and cook 1 minute.
Return the steak, add the fries and cilantro and toss gently to coat everything in the sauce. Serve with rice if you like.

items.title: Reverse-Seared Steak

source.name: Serious Eats · recipe by J. Kenji López-Alt

items.note: Low and slow first, sear last: the steak comes out evenly cooked from edge to edge, with a crisp crust and no need to rest.

items: Thick-cut steak(s), 1½–2 inches thick, such as rib-eye, strip, porterhouse, T-bone, tri-tip or filet mignon
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tbsp vegetable oil (for the stovetop finish)

steps.text: Season the steaks generously all over with salt and pepper. If you have time, set them on a wire rack in a rimmed baking sheet and refrigerate overnight, uncovered, to dry the surface.
Heat the oven to anywhere from 200 to 275°F (93–135°C). An even lower setting works too; it just takes longer.

Set the steaks on a wire rack in a rimmed baking sheet and cook until an instant-read thermometer reads 105°F (41°C) for rare, 115°F (46°C) for medium-rare, 125°F (52°C) for medium or 135°F (57°C) for medium-well. Figure about 20 minutes for rare and up to 40 for medium-well, but times vary a lot, so check often.

Just before the steaks are done, heat the oil in a cast-iron, carbon-steel or heavy stainless skillet over high heat until it smokes. Add the steaks and the butter and sear until well browned, about 45 seconds per side. Hold each steak on its side with tongs to sear the edges, then serve right away.

Season the steaks as above. Light a full chimney of charcoal, and when the coals are covered in gray ash, spread them over half the grate (on a gas grill, turn half the burners to high). Set the cooking grate in place, cover and preheat for 5 minutes, then clean and oil the grate.
Cook the steaks on the cooler side, uncovered, turning now and then, until they reach the same temperatures as above. Check them often.

Move the steaks to a platter and tent with foil. Build the charcoal fire up as hot as you can (or turn every gas burner to high and preheat with the lid closed), then sear the steaks over the hottest part, turning often, until crisp and charred all over, about 1½ minutes total. Serve right away.

items.title: Rosemary Braised Lamb Shanks

items: 3 large carrots, sliced into ¼-inch rounds
1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, with juice

steps.text: Season the shanks with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the shanks on all sides in batches, about 8 minutes, then set them aside on a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the carrots, onions and garlic and cook about 10 minutes, until golden, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in the wine, tomatoes, both broths, the rosemary and thyme.
Nestle the shanks back into the liquid and bring to a boil. Turn the heat to medium-low, cover and simmer about 2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Uncover and simmer 20 minutes more to concentrate the flavor. Move the shanks to a platter and keep them warm under foil.
Boil the sauce about 15 minutes, until thickened, and spoon it over the shanks.

tips: For a one-pot meal, add 1 lb small potatoes to the pot for the last 45 minutes instead of serving with mash.

items: 1 rabbit (about 3 lb), cleaned and cut into pieces

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Season the rabbit with the pepper and salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the rabbit on all sides. Move it to a 9 × 13 baking dish.
Stir together the onion, water, ketchup, Worcestershire, sugar, paprika and garlic and pour it over the rabbit.
Bake uncovered about 90 minutes, basting often, until very tender and at least 160°F (71°C) near the bone.

chapters.title: Pork
chapters.blurb: Pulled pork and carnitas, a one-pot Instant Pot pork roast with sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts, breaded chops and two kinds of ribs.

items.title: Instant Pot Roast Pork with Brussels Sprouts and Sweet Potatoes
items.note: A whole dinner from one pot: paprika-rubbed pork shoulder pressure-cooked on a bed of onions and tarragon, then sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts cooked in the same broth.

items: 2½ lb boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), trimmed and cut into 4 pieces
⅝ tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
1½ lb peeled sweet potatoes, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved

steps.text: Pat the pork dry with paper towels. Mix the paprika, ½ tsp of the salt, ½ tsp of the pepper and the garlic, and rub it all over the pork.
Set a 6-quart Instant Pot to Sauté (More). Add 2 tsp of the oil and brown the pork on all sides, about 8 minutes. Move it to a plate.

Add the remaining 1 tsp oil and the onion wedges and cook, stirring constantly, until lightly browned, about 3 minutes. Stir in the water, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Set the pork on top of the onions, scatter over the tarragon and turn off Sauté.
Lock the lid, set the valve to Sealing and cook at High Pressure for 32 minutes. Quick-release the pressure, lift out the pork and keep it warm.
Add the sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts to the onion broth in the pot. Lock the lid and cook at High Pressure for 4 minutes, then quick-release.
Lift the vegetables onto a platter with a slotted spoon and sprinkle with the remaining ¼ tsp salt. Don't toss them, or the sweet potatoes will fall apart.
Shred the pork into bite-size pieces and pile it next to the vegetables. Sprinkle with the remaining ⅛ tsp pepper and serve with the honey mustard.

items.title: Italian Breaded Pork Chops

steps.text: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C).
Beat the eggs and milk in a shallow dish. Mix the breadcrumbs, Parmesan and parsley in a second dish.
Dip each chop in the egg, then coat it well in the crumbs.
Heat the oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic until just golden to flavor the oil, then lift it out (save it for another use).
Fry the chops about 5 minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake 20–25 minutes, until the chops reach 145°F (63°C) in the center.

tips: No ovenproof skillet? Finish the chops on the stove over medium-low heat instead.
For a thicker crust, dip the chops in egg and crumbs twice. A white wine and lemon butter sauce dresses them up.

items: ½ cup BBQ sauce, plus more to taste

steps.text: Cut the pork shoulder into two roughly 1-lb pieces.
Mix the onion powder, garlic powder, mustard, salt and pepper and rub it all over the pork.
Put the pork in the pressure cooker and pour in the BBQ sauce and water.
Lock the lid, set the valve to Sealing and cook on High pressure for 40 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then vent the rest.
Lift the pork out (leave the liquid behind) and shred it with two forks. Toss with extra BBQ sauce to taste.
Put the ribs in a large pot, cover with water and stir in the salt, garlic powder and pepper. Bring to a boil over medium heat and boil 40–45 minutes, until tender.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Move the ribs to a 9 × 13 baking dish, pour the barbecue sauce over them and cover with foil.
Bake 1–1½ hours, until the pork reaches 160°F (71°C).

items.title: Slow Cooker Carnitas

items: 4 lb (2 kg) boneless, skinless pork shoulder (or 5 lb / 2.5 kg bone-in)

steps.text: Pat the pork dry and season it all over with the salt and pepper.
Mix the oregano, cumin and olive oil and rub it over the pork.
Set the pork in the slow cooker fat-side up. Scatter over the onion, jalapeño and garlic, then pour over the orange juice.
Cook on Low for 10 hours or High for 7 hours, until it shreds easily.

Lift out the pork, let it cool slightly and shred it with two forks. Skim the fat off the juices if you like. If there's more than 2 cups of juice, boil it down to about 2 cups and keep it (unstrained) for seasoning.

**To crisp:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick or well-seasoned skillet over high heat. Spread out a batch of pork, drizzle with some of the juice and leave it until the juice cooks off and the underside is golden and crusty. Flip and sear the other side briefly. Repeat in batches without crowding the pan.
Drizzle with a little more juice just before serving.

tips: Leave some of the fat cap on (but remove any skin); you can skim the fat later.
Smaller roast (2–3 lb boneless): 8 hours on Low.
**Instant Pot:** 1 hr 30 min at High pressure with natural release, then shred and crisp as above.
**Oven:** In a covered roasting pan with 2 cups water at 325°F (160°C) for 2 hours, then uncovered for 1–1½ hours more, adding water if needed. No need to pan-fry afterwards.
Store the pork and juices separately: 3 days in the fridge, 3 months in the freezer.

steps.text: Mix the rub ingredients and coat the ribs. If you have time, let them sit for up to an hour.
Grease the slow cooker and scatter the onion over the bottom. Lay the ribs on top.
Stir together the broth, vinegar, Worcestershire and liquid smoke and pour it over the ribs.
Cook on Low for 4 hours.
Lift the ribs out carefully, since they'll be very tender, and serve with the cooking juices or your favorite BBQ sauce.

chapters.title: Fish & Seafood
chapters.blurb: Seared ahi, broiled halibut, cracker-topped cod, shrimp ceviche, shrimp and grits, miso black cod, lemon garlic swordfish, and two whole fish: snapper baked in foil and Cantonese steamed fish.

items.title: Baked Whole Red Snapper with Garlic

source.name: Epicurious · from the Admiral's Inn, Antigua

items.note: An easy but impressive whole fish from the Admiral's Inn in Antigua, baked in a sealed foil packet with garlic, lemon and thyme. Have the fish market clean and scale the snapper for you.

items: 2 tbsp (¼ stick) chilled butter, cut into pieces, plus more for the foil

steps.text: Lay a 24 × 18-inch sheet of foil on a large, heavy baking sheet and butter it. Set the fish in the center.
Season the cavity with the garlic, lemon juice and seafood seasoning, dot it with the butter and tuck in the thyme sprigs.
Sprinkle the outside of the fish with salt and pepper and lay the lemon slices on top. Fold the edges of the foil over the fish and seal. (You can get this far a day ahead; keep it refrigerated.)
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake until the fish is cooked through, about 45 minutes.
Transfer the fish to a platter and open the foil.

tips: Can't find a whole snapper? Use fillets and bake them about 25 minutes.

items.title: Cantonese Steamed Fish

ingredients.title: Fish and marinade
items: 1 whole white fish, 1.2–1.8 lb (544–820 g) before gutting (snapper, perch, sea bass), scaled and gutted

ingredients.title: Seasoned soy sauce
items: ½ dried shiitake mushroom, snipped into pieces

ingredients.title: To steam and finish
items: 3-inch piece of ginger (45 g), cut into thick strips
4 scallions (60 g), cut into 3-inch lengths, whites and greens separated

steps.text: Rinse the cleaned fish well. Cut along the backbone on both sides (and score the thick fillets once or twice if you like) so it cooks evenly.
Roughly chop the crushed garlic, ginger and scallions and rub them over the fish with the wine. Leave at room temperature while you make the sauce.

**Sauce:** Soak the shiitake in the hot water for 15 minutes. Warm the oil and Sichuan peppercorns in a small saucepan over low heat for 1 minute. Add the diced ginger, garlic and scallion and stir over medium-low for 3 minutes. Add the soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and the mushroom with its soaking water. Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 3 minutes. Strain if you want it smooth.

Lay the ginger strips and scallion whites on a heatproof plate to make a rack. Finely julienne the scallion greens, ginger slices and chili, soak them in cold water for at least 10 minutes so they curl, then pat dry.
Fill your largest steamer with plenty of water and bring it to a full boil over the highest heat. Discard the marinade aromatics, pat the fish dry and set it on the ginger-scallion rack.

Steam over the highest heat: 6–8 minutes for a 1.2-lb fish, 7–9 for 1.4 lb, 8–10 for 1.6 lb and 10–12 for 1.8 lb. Turn off the heat and leave the lid on 3–5 minutes more. A chopstick should slide into the thickest part with no resistance.

Move the fish to a clean platter, leaving the steaming liquid behind. Top with the minced garlic and the julienned aromatics. Heat the 3 tbsp oil until smoking and pour it over the aromatics, then spoon the seasoned soy sauce around the fish. Serve with rice.

tips: Freshness is everything: look for clear, shiny eyes, red gills, glossy skin and a clean smell.
Steam it in one go. Opening the steamer to check partway through hurts the texture.
Bottled "seasoned soy sauce for seafood" (蒸鱼豉油) can replace the homemade sauce.

items.title: Easy Shrimp Ceviche
items.time: Prep 15 min · Cook 5 min, plus 20 min in lime juice

items: 2 serrano peppers, seeded, deveined and finely chopped
½ lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: Combine the cucumber, tomatoes, onion, serranos and cilantro in a bowl. Add 1 tsp of the salt and the juice of 1 lime, mix gently and set aside.
Squeeze the remaining 5 limes into another bowl and add the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Drop in the shrimp for 45 seconds, then scoop them out with a strainer.
Chop the partly cooked shrimp into small pieces and stir them into the seasoned lime juice. Let sit 20 minutes.
Combine with the vegetable mixture and top with the avocado.

tips: Unlike fish ceviche, shrimp shouldn't sit in citrus for hours. The quick blanch gives them a firmer texture and lowers the risk that comes with raw seafood.

items: Fresh herbs and lemon slices, to garnish (optional)

steps.text: Set a rack about 6 inches below the broiler and heat it. Grease a rimmed baking sheet and lay the halibut on it.
Broil about 8 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Meanwhile, mix the Parmesan, butter, mayonnaise, green onions, lemon juice, salt and hot sauce.
Spread the topping over the fish and broil about 2 minutes more, until bubbling and lightly browned.
Garnish with herbs and lemon slices, if you like, and serve hot.

ingredients.title: Fish
items: 2 swordfish steaks, 1 inch thick (6–7 oz each)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) with a rack in the middle. Stir the lemon garlic butter ingredients together in a small pan and set aside.
Pat the swordfish dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the fish about 3 minutes without moving it, until browned underneath. Flip, turn off the burner and move the pan straight into the oven.
Roast 5–6 minutes, until the center is just cooked through. Don't overcook it.
About a minute before the fish is ready, set the lemon garlic butter over medium-high heat and stir until melted and bubbling. Pour it over the fish, along with any juices from the pan.

items: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1¼ lb medium shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on
Juice of ½ lemon, plus wedges to serve

steps.text: Bring 3 cups of water to a boil in a covered medium saucepan. Uncover and slowly whisk in the grits, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper. Turn the heat to medium-low and cook about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Stir in the Parmesan and 1 tbsp of the butter, season to taste, then cover and keep warm off the heat.

Season the shrimp with salt and pepper. Melt the remaining 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp, garlic and cayenne and toss for 3–4 minutes, until the shrimp are pink.
Take the pan off the heat and add 2 tbsp water, the lemon juice and the parsley. Toss to coat and season to taste.
Spoon the grits into shallow bowls, top with the shrimp and pan sauce and serve with lemon wedges.

items.title: Nobu-Style Miso Black Cod
items.time: Prep 10 min, plus 2–3 days marinating · Cook 10–14 min

source.name: The Kitchn (adapted from Nobu: The Cookbook)

items: 4 black cod (sablefish) fillets, 4–6 oz each, center-cut if possible
Cooking spray, or 2 tbsp vegetable or canola oil

steps.text: **Two to three days ahead:** Bring the sake and mirin to a boil in a small saucepan over high heat and let it bubble for 20 seconds to cook off the alcohol. Turn the heat to low, whisk in the miso and sugar until dissolved, then cool to room temperature.
Pat the fillets dry and lay them snugly in a zip-top bag or container. Pour in the marinade, turn to coat, seal and refrigerate for 2–3 days.
When ready to cook, lift the fish out and wipe off the excess marinade with your fingers, leaving a thin film (don't rinse it). Season lightly with salt. Cook by either method below.

**Broiler:** Set a rack 6–8 inches below the broiler and heat it. Cover a wire rack with foil, set it on a baking sheet and spray the foil. Lay the fish skin-side down and broil 8–12 minutes, checking often and rotating the pan, until it flakes and the top is deep golden with charred spots.

**Sear and bake:** Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Heat the oil in a 12-inch ovenproof skillet (cast iron is best) over medium-high until it just starts to smoke. Add the fish skin-side up and sear 2–3 minutes, until browned and blackened in spots. Flip with a thin metal spatula, sear 2–3 minutes more, then bake 5–10 minutes until opaque and flaky.
Lift onto plates with a thin spatula and pull out any pin bones before serving.

tips: The sugar in the marinade scorches quickly, so stay close to the broiler.

items: ½ sleeve buttery round crackers (such as Ritz), crushed

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Microwave 2 tbsp of the butter in a bowl for about 30 seconds, until melted, and stir in the crushed crackers.
Put the remaining 2 tbsp butter in a 7 × 11 baking dish and melt it in the oven, 1–3 minutes. Add the cod and turn it to coat in the butter.
Bake 10 minutes. Pour the wine and lemon juice over the fish, top with the cracker mixture and bake about 10 minutes more, until opaque and flaky.
Sprinkle with the parsley and green onion and serve with lemon wedges.

items.title: Seared Ahi Tuna Steaks

steps.text: Pat the tuna dry and season both sides with the salt and cayenne.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat, add the oil and peppercorns and cook about 5 minutes, until the peppercorns soften and pop.
Lay the tuna in the pan and sear 30 seconds to 1½ minutes per side, depending on how rare you like it.
Slice ¼ inch thick to serve.

tips: If you like your tuna rare, buy sushi-grade.

chapters.title: Pasta & Casseroles
chapters.blurb: A classic meat lasagna, a creamy tortellini bake, a lighter cottage cheese Alfredo and an old-school chicken, broccoli and rice casserole.

items.title: Broccoli, Rice, Cheese, and Chicken Casserole

items: 2 cans (10 oz each) chunk chicken, drained
1 lb processed cheese (such as Velveeta), cubed
1 can (10.75 oz) condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 can (10.75 oz) condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan, stir in the rice, cover and take it off the heat. Let stand 5 minutes.
Combine the rice, chicken, broccoli, cheese, both soups, milk, butter and onion in a 9 × 13 baking dish.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until the cheese has melted, stirring halfway through so it melts evenly.

tips: It halves well. The author uses just one can of cream of mushroom soup for a half batch.

items: 1½ cups shredded mozzarella or Monterey Jack

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9 × 13 baking dish.

Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and brown the chicken for 3–4 minutes. Add the mushrooms, green onions and garlic and cook until the chicken is cooked through and the mushrooms are golden.
Sprinkle the flour over everything, stir well and cook for 1–2 minutes. Stir in the broth and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Stir in the sour cream, season with salt and pepper, then fold in the uncooked tortellini.
Spread the mixture in the dish and top with the cheese. Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes more, until bubbling and golden at the edges.

items.title: Cottage Cheese Alfredo
items.note: Bookmarked as "Skinny Alfredo." A lighter fettuccine Alfredo: the creamy sauce is cottage cheese and milk blended smooth, with baby spinach and plenty of Parmesan, so it's lower in fat and high in protein.

items: 1 oz Parmesan, shredded (about ⅓ cup packed)

steps.text: Cook the fettuccine in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring now and then, until very al dente, about 1 minute less than the package says. Save ½ cup of the pasta water, then drain. Toss the pasta with the oil in a large bowl.
Meanwhile, blend the cottage cheese, milk, Parmesan, garlic, butter, flour and 1 tsp salt in a blender or food processor until smooth.
Pour the sauce into a large skillet and bring it to a simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring often with a heatproof spatula, until thickened, 8–10 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Add the pasta to the skillet and toss to coat, loosening the sauce with some of the pasta water if it gets too thick.
Divide among bowls and sprinkle with red pepper flakes.

items.title: World's Best Lasagna

steps.text: Brown the sausage, beef, onion and garlic in a Dutch oven over medium heat.

Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste and water. Season with the sugar, 2 tbsp of the parsley, the basil, 1 tsp of the salt, the Italian seasoning, fennel seeds and pepper. Cover and simmer about 1½ hours, stirring occasionally.
Boil the noodles in lightly salted water for 8–10 minutes. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Mix the ricotta with the egg, the remaining 2 tbsp parsley and ½ tsp salt.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

Spread 1½ cups of the sauce in a 9 × 13 baking dish. Lay 6 noodles lengthwise on top, slightly overlapping. Spread with half the ricotta mixture, then a third of the mozzarella. Spoon over 1½ cups sauce and sprinkle with ¼ cup Parmesan.
Repeat the layers, then finish with the rest of the mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover with foil (spray it, or tent it so it doesn't touch the cheese) and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 25 minutes more.
Rest 15 minutes before cutting so it sets.

tips: The recipe's video uses three layers of 4 noodles that don't overlap. Done that way, use 1 cup sauce and a third of the ricotta per layer.

chapters.title: Thai Curries
chapters.blurb: Red, panang and choo chee curries, from a weeknight chicken curry to whole mackerel.

items.title: Choo Chee Mackerel (Fillets)

items: ¼ cup plus ⅔ cup coconut milk
3 makrut (kaffir) lime leaves, center rib removed, finely julienned
Julienned red spur chili or red bell pepper, to garnish (optional)
1–2 tbsp extra coconut milk, to garnish (optional)

steps.text: Bring ¼ cup coconut milk to a boil in a wok or wide sauté pan.
Add the curry paste and stir constantly until it's thick and the coconut oil starts to separate (if it doesn't separate, carry on anyway).
Add the remaining ⅔ cup coconut milk, the palm sugar and fish sauce and simmer a few minutes, until thick and rich but still pourable.
Stir in half the lime leaves and let them infuse for about a minute. Season the sauce boldly, since it mellows once it's served with the fish and rice. Set aside, covered.
Pat the fish dry. Heat a thin layer of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear skin-side down about 2 minutes, until golden, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
Bring the sauce back to a boil, thinning with a splash of water if needed. Add the fish skin-side up and simmer 30 seconds to 1 minute, keeping the sauce off the crisp skin.
Plate the fish, pour the sauce around it and over the flesh, then drizzle with the extra coconut milk and top with the rest of the lime leaves and the chili.

tips: Making your own curry paste? Halve the salt and shrimp paste.

items: 700 g (about 1½ lb) whole fresh mackerel, cleaned
¾ cup coconut milk, plus a little extra to garnish
2 makrut (kaffir) lime leaves, center rib removed, torn
50 g (about ¼ cup) palm sugar, or brown or white sugar
4 makrut lime leaves, finely shredded, to garnish
1 red chili, cut into thin strips, to garnish

steps.text: Gut and clean the mackerel, rinse well and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the curry paste for 1–2 minutes.
Add half the coconut milk and fry until fragrant, then add the torn lime leaves, fish sauce and sugar and stir.
When it boils, add the rest of the coconut milk and bring back to a boil over high heat.
Add the mackerel and turn the heat to medium-low. Spoon the sauce over the fish (a wide pan keeps the fish from being drowned). Cover and cook 15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer 3–5 minutes more to thicken the sauce, basting the fish again.
Garnish with the shredded lime leaves, chili and a drizzle of coconut milk, and serve with steamed rice.

items.title: Panang Curry

items: 2 lb chicken breasts, cut across the grain into bite-size pieces
¼ cup packed light brown sugar
1 cup loosely packed basil leaves, roughly chopped

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion 2 minutes, then add the peppers, garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes more.
Stir in the curry paste and peanut butter for 1 minute. Add 1½ cans of the coconut milk. Whisk the cornstarch into the remaining half can and stir it in.
Add the chicken and simmer 10–15 minutes, until cooked through and the sauce begins to thicken.
Stir in the brown sugar, fish sauce, lime juice and basil and simmer 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and serve over rice.

tips: Mae Ploy paste is recommended. 2 tbsp is medium-hot; add chili sauce at the end if you want more heat.
Mushrooms, zucchini, bamboo shoots, spinach or carrots all work, and so do shrimp or tofu instead of chicken.
Keeps 5–7 days in the fridge or 2–3 months in the freezer.

items.title: Salmon Coconut Curry

items: 2 heaping tbsp Thai red curry paste
½ tsp fish sauce (optional but recommended)

steps.text: Cut the salmon into 4 pieces, pat dry and season with salt and pepper.

Heat the oil and butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the salmon skin-side down for 5 minutes (let it release on its own), then flip and cook 2–3 minutes more, until almost done. Move it to a plate and slip off the skin if you like.
Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat. Cook the onion about 3 minutes, until lightly browned, then stir in the garlic and curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the fish sauce, coconut milk, brown sugar, carrots and broccolini and simmer gently about 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in the lime juice, nestle the salmon back in and warm through for a couple of minutes. Season to taste and top with the basil and cilantro.

tips: Thai Kitchen curry paste and coconut milk are recommended; that brand's coconut milk is extra thick.
Soy sauce can stand in for fish sauce, though the flavor changes. Regular broccoli works if you cut it small.

items.title: Thai Red Curry with Chicken

ingredients.title: Curry paste (choose one)
items: 5–6 tbsp store-bought Thai red curry paste (Maesri recommended)
or 1 batch homemade red curry paste

ingredients.title: Extras, for jar paste only
items: 1 tbsp lemongrass paste (or 2 tsp finely minced fresh lemongrass)

ingredients.title: Curry
items: 1 can (400 ml / 14 oz) full-fat coconut milk
2 tsp fish sauce, plus more to taste
350 g (12 oz) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, sliced about ⅓ inch thick
150 g (5 oz) pumpkin or butternut squash, in 1.5 cm (generous ½-inch) cubes
120 g (4 oz) green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
Sliced red chili, cilantro and jasmine rice, to serve

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the curry paste (and the extras, if using jar paste) and cook about 2 minutes to dry it out.
Pour in the broth, stir to dissolve the paste and simmer hard for 3 minutes, until reduced by half.
Stir in the coconut milk, lime leaves, sugar and fish sauce, then add the chicken and spread it out.
Bring to a simmer, lower the heat to medium and cook 8–10 minutes, until the chicken is done and the sauce has reduced.
Taste: add fish sauce for saltiness or sugar for sweetness.
Add the squash and green beans and cook 3 minutes, until the squash is just tender and the sauce has thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the basil. Serve over jasmine rice with chili and cilantro.

tips: Jar paste is much stronger than homemade. With Maesri, 5 tbsp is medium-hot and 6 tbsp is spicy.
A little oil pooling on the surface is normal for Thai curry.
Thigh stays juiciest, but breast or tenderloin also works. Regular basil can stand in for Thai basil; use just a small handful.

chapters.title: Asian Kitchen
chapters.blurb: Sushi rice and California rolls, baked katsu, dim sum chicken feet, creamy Korean rice cakes and a Thai squash stir-fry.

items.title: Baked Chicken Katsu

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) with a rack in the middle (25°F lower for convection).
Toast the panko with the oil in a frying pan over medium heat, stirring often, until golden. Tip into a shallow dish to cool.

Butterfly each breast: cut a slit down the center lengthwise without cutting all the way through, open the sides out like a book, then cut in half to make two cutlets. Pound them to an even ¼–½ inch thickness.
Season both sides with salt (use half as much if it's table salt) and pepper.
Set out three shallow dishes: the egg beaten with the ½ tbsp oil, the flour, and the toasted panko.
Coat each cutlet in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in egg, then press it firmly into the panko.
Arrange on a wire rack set over a rimmed baking sheet and bake 25–30 minutes, until 165°F (74°C) inside.
Slice into ¾-inch strips and serve with tonkatsu sauce.

tips: Toasting the panko first gives the deep golden color of fried katsu without the frying.
Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge or 1 month frozen. Reheat at 350°F for 15–20 minutes (about 30 minutes from frozen).

items.title: California Rolls
items.time: 20 min, plus making the sushi rice

items: 1 batch sushi rice (see Perfect Sushi Rice in this chapter)
1 medium avocado, cut into 16–20 thin wedges
1 small cucumber, seeded and cut into thin strips (about ⅕ inch)
200 g (7 oz) crab meat or imitation crab
1 tbsp rice vinegar stirred into 1 cup water, for your hands
Soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger, to serve

steps.text: Stir the vinegar into the water to make a hand-dip. If using a bamboo mat, wrap it in plastic wrap.

Lay a half-sheet of nori on the mat near the edge closest to you. With damp fingers, spread a generous handful of rice evenly over the nori, leaving a ¼-inch strip bare along the far edge. Spread gently so you don't crush the grains.
Sprinkle the rice with sesame seeds, then flip the sheet over so the rice faces down and the bare strip is nearest you.
Lay avocado wedges across the middle of the nori, overlapping the thin ends, then add a cucumber strip and the crab. Don't overfill (split imitation crab sticks lengthwise if needed).

Tuck your thumbs under the mat, hold the filling with your fingers and roll away from you until the edge of the rice meets the bare nori. Press lightly to seal and keep rolling until the seam is underneath.
Squeeze the roll gently through the mat, top and sides, to firm it up evenly.
With a sharp, wet knife and a back-and-forth sawing motion, cut the roll in half. Line up the halves and cut them into 4 pieces each.
Serve with soy sauce, wasabi and ginger.

items: 2 cups tteokbokki rice cakes (thawed if frozen)
A few sausages, sliced into rounds (or 2 strips bacon)
1 sheet fish cake, cut into bite-size pieces (optional)

ingredients.title: Creamy sauce
items: A few grinds of black pepper
1 slice sandwich cheese (or a handful of shredded cheese)

steps.text: If the rice cakes are frozen, soak them in water to thaw while you prep everything else.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch the broccoli for 30 seconds and scoop it out. Lower the eggs into the same water and boil 7 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Drain the rice cakes. Heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium heat and stir-fry the garlic, onion and sausage until the onion is translucent.
Pour in the cream and milk and stir in the gochujang and gochugaru. Add the rice cakes and let it bubble a few minutes, until they soften.
Add the broccoli, the eggs and the fish cake, and season with salt and pepper. Stir in the cheese and simmer until the sauce is thick and creamy.
Serve topped with a little grated Parmesan.

items.title: Dim Sum Chicken Feet (Pressure Cooker)
items.time: Prep 10 min · Cook 45 min, plus 1–2 hr soaking

items: Oil, for frying (or for coating if air-frying or baking)

ingredients.title: Braise
items: ¼ cup rock sugar (or 1 tbsp granulated or brown sugar)

ingredients.title: To finish
items: 2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water (optional)

steps.text: Clip the nails off the feet and cut away any discolored spots. Rub all over with the salt, rinse, and pat completely dry.
Fry until golden, by one of these methods:
sub: **Deep-fry:** in batches in hot oil for about 5 minutes, until pale golden. Use a lid; they spatter.
**Air fryer:** coat in oil and air-fry at 400°F (200°C) for 15 minutes, shake, then 15 minutes more.
**Oven:** coat in oil and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.text: If deep-fried, drop them straight into ice water and soak 1–2 hours, until puffed. This gives the wrinkly dim-sum texture.
On Sauté, heat 1 tbsp oil in the pressure cooker. Cook the garlic and ginger 1 minute, add the star anise for 30 seconds, then deglaze with the Shaoxing wine, scraping the bottom.
Add the feet, oyster sauce, both soy sauces, sugar and chilies and stir. Pour in water just to cover.
Pressure cook on High for 35 minutes (add 3–5 minutes if they're not tender enough), then let the pressure release naturally.
Switch to Sauté, bring to a boil and stir in the cornstarch slurry to lightly thicken the sauce. Scatter with green onion and serve.

tips: **Stovetop:** Follow the same steps in a covered pot and simmer gently for 1½–2 hours, until tender.

items.title: Kabocha Squash Stir-Fry (Pad Faktong)

items: 500 g (about 1 lb) kabocha squash, cut into 1-inch wedges, then into ¼-inch slices
Prik nam pla (chili fish sauce), to serve (optional)

ingredients.title: Sauce
items: ¼ tsp ground white (or black) pepper

ingredients.title: Vegetarian sauce (instead)
items: 2 tsp Golden Mountain sauce (or Maggi Seasoning)
¼ tsp ground white (or black) pepper

steps.text: Stir the sauce ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a wok and cook the garlic until it just starts to turn golden.

Add the squash and toss to coat in the oil, then add the sauce and toss again. Cover and cook over medium heat about 4 minutes, stirring once, until a fork goes through a piece with slight resistance. Add a splash of water if it dries out.

Push the squash aside to clear a space in the middle. Crack in the eggs and break up the yolks. Lay the squash back over the eggs and let them set without stirring; when they're about 75% cooked, toss gently once or twice so the egg stays in chunks.
Once the eggs are cooked, turn off the heat and stir in the basil until just wilted. Serve with rice and a drizzle of prik nam pla.

tips: Don't slice the squash thinner than ¼ inch, or it overcooks and falls apart.

items.title: Perfect Sushi Rice
items.time: Prep 5 min · Cook 20 min, plus cooling

steps.text: Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water until the water runs clear.

Bring the rice and water to a boil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Turn the heat to low, cover and cook 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes more to finish steaming. Uncover and let cool.
Meanwhile, warm the vinegar, sugar, oil and salt in a small saucepan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves. Let cool.
Stir the vinegar mixture into the rice. It looks wet at first but dries as it cools.

tips: Allrecipes' test kitchen cut the vinegar to ¼ cup; the original recipe uses ½ cup.
Use it for the California Rolls in this chapter.

chapters.title: Soups, Stews & Stock
chapters.blurb: Chili, chowder, three stews, a 15-minute egg drop soup and a pressure cooker stock to build on.

items.title: Creamy Chicken and Corn Chowder

items: 3 cups cooked shredded chicken (rotisserie works well)
1 large red bell pepper, diced (1½ cups)
1–2 jalapeños, finely chopped (seeded for less heat)
3 medium russet potatoes (22 oz), peeled and cut just under ½ inch (3 cups)
Green onions and shredded cheese, to serve (optional)

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the bell pepper, onion and jalapeño and cook about 3 minutes, until tender.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually stir in the broth. Add the potatoes and bay leaves and season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, stirring often, then turn the heat to low and simmer uncovered 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the chicken, corn and half-and-half and simmer 5 minutes more. Fish out the bay leaves.
Serve topped with the bacon, plus green onions and cheese if you like.

tips: Starting with raw chicken? Add about 1 lb of breasts or thighs with the potatoes, cook until 165°F (74°C), then shred and return to the pot.

items: ½ tsp ground turmeric (optional, for color)
3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with ⅓ cup water

steps.text: Bring the stock to a simmer in a medium pot. Stir in the sesame oil, salt, sugar, white pepper and MSG, if using.
Add the turmeric for color, if using. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Re-stir the cornstarch slurry (it settles fast), then drizzle it in slowly while stirring constantly. Add more or less for a thicker or thinner soup, simmering a minute or two between additions.
Stir the soup in a circle with a ladle and slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream. Stir faster for fine ribbons, slower for big ones.
Ladle into bowls and top with the scallion.

items.title: Instant Pot Fish Stew
items.time: Prep 5 min · Cook 15 min, plus 10 min to come to pressure

items: 1 medium red onion, quartered and thinly sliced
½ cup dry white wine (such as pinot grigio or sauvignon blanc)
½ lb red or gold potatoes, diced
1 can (15 oz) diced tomatoes, or 1½ cups diced fresh tomatoes with their juice
2 lb sea bass, cut into roughly 2-inch pieces

steps.text: On the Sauté setting, cook the onion in 2 tbsp of the oil for about 3 minutes, until softened and browned.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble about 1 minute, until reduced by half.
Add the clam juice, water, potatoes, tomatoes, plenty of salt and pepper and the crushed red pepper.
Turn off Sauté, seal the lid and cook at High pressure for 5 minutes. Quick-release the pressure.
Switch back to Sauté. When the stew simmers, add the fish and simmer about 5 minutes, until it just flakes apart.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, dill and the remaining 2 tbsp oil. Season to taste and serve with crusty bread.

tips: Any firm white fish works: cod, monkfish or halibut.
**Stovetop:** Start the same way in a large pot, then simmer covered about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Add the fish for the last 5 minutes.

**Slow cooker:** Add everything except the fish, lemon juice, dill and final 2 tbsp oil. Cook on Low 6 hours or High 3 hours, add the fish for the last 20 minutes, then stir in the finishing ingredients.
No clam juice (or a shellfish allergy)? Use fish stock, or one more cup of water.
Written for a 6-quart pot; halve it for a 3-quart mini.

items.title: Mallard Creek Brunswick Stew
items.time: Two days (meat is cooked and chilled overnight)

steps.text: **Day 1:** Simmer the beef, pork and hen in water (together or separately) until tender. Save the broth. Let the meat cool, then remove the bones and the chicken skin.
Grind all the meat in a food processor or meat grinder. Refrigerate the meat and the broth overnight.
**Day 2:** Strain the broth into a large pot. Add the rice, butter, salt and pepper and cook about 30 minutes, stirring constantly, until the rice is tender.
Add the tomatoes and corn. Once it's back to a simmer, cook about 20 minutes.
Stir in the ground meat and cook 10 minutes more. Stir often, adding hot water if the stew starts to stick.

tips: The original also gives a larger batch, cooked the same way: 6 lb beef chuck, a 5-lb hen, 1 lb rice, 2 cans creamed corn, 2 cans lima beans, 3 large cans stewed tomatoes, 6 chopped onions, ¼ cup salt, 1 tbsp pepper and up to 1 lb butter (optional).
This makes a big batch, and it freezes well in pint containers.

items.title: Pressure Cooker Roast Chicken Stock

items: ½ carrot, peeled and thinly sliced
1–2 tbsp chicken fat or neutral oil

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a kettle or separate pot.
Heat the fat in the pressure cooker on Sauté and sweat the carrot, onion and garlic until soft and lightly colored.
Meanwhile, strip all the meat off the chicken and shred it finely. Add the shredded meat, skin and carcass to the pot. (More surface area means faster, fuller extraction.)
Pour in the boiling water, seal, and bring to High pressure. Cook 40 minutes; 30–90 minutes is the sweet spot for chicken.
Don't quick-release. Let the pressure drop naturally (or release it very slowly) so the stock doesn't churn and turn cloudy.
Strain through a fine sieve. Chill, then lift off the fat.

tips: For beef stock, go about 2 hours. Past roughly 3 hours under pressure, stock turns metallic and bitter and won't set to a gel.

**Crystal-clear consommé, the easy way:** freeze the stock in cubes, then let them thaw slowly in a lined strainer set over a bowl in the fridge. The liquid that drips through is clear; the fat and haze stay behind.

**Raft method:** blend some of the stock with a little raw chicken until frothy, stir it back into the pot, bring to High pressure, then let it cool naturally. A raft forms on top and traps the cloudiness; strain through a sieve.

items.title: Savory Pork Stew

items: 1 can (10.75 oz) condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Season the pork all over with garlic powder, salt and pepper, then dust it lightly with cornstarch. Brown it lightly in the hot oil; it doesn't need to cook through.
Move the pork to a slow cooker and add the potatoes, bell peppers, onion and corn.
Mix the tomatoes, broth, mushroom soup, milk and Italian seasoning in a bowl and pour it into the slow cooker.
Cook on High for 1 hour, then on Low for at least 1 hour more.

tips: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

items.title: The Best Chili

items: 1 can (19 oz) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, with juice
Shredded cheddar, green onions and cilantro, to serve

steps.text: Mix the beef with 1½ tbsp of the chili powder.
Brown the beef with the onion, jalapeño and garlic in a large pot, then drain off the fat.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp chili powder, the cumin, bell pepper, both cans of tomatoes, beans, broth, beer, tomato paste and sugar. Bring to a boil.
Turn down the heat and simmer uncovered 45–60 minutes, until it's as thick as you like. Season with salt and pepper and serve with your favorite toppings.

tips: Swap the beer for more beef broth if you prefer.
Any ground meat works here.

chapters.title: Vegetables & Sides
chapters.blurb: Sausage-stuffed zucchini boats, eggplant Parmesan and pesto spaghetti squash, two kinds of mashed potatoes, two sweet potato casseroles and a green bean casserole for the holidays, Korean potato salad and a very cheesy potato bake.

items.title: Best Green Bean Casserole

items: 2 cans (14.5 oz each) green beans, drained well
1 can (10.5 oz) condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix the green beans and soup in a large microwave-safe bowl and microwave on High 3–5 minutes, until warm.
Stir in ½ cup of the Cheddar and microwave 2–3 minutes more, until hot.
Spread in a 1½-quart casserole dish, sprinkle with the remaining Cheddar and top with the fried onions.
Bake about 10 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and the onions are lightly browned. Watch the onions near the end so they don't burn.

tips: A 16-oz bag of frozen cut green beans, thawed and drained, can replace the cans.
For extra crunch, hold back a handful of onions and add them for the last few minutes.
To make ahead, assemble without the onions up to a day early and refrigerate. Add the onions just before baking and allow a little extra time.

items.title: Best Mashed Potatoes

items: 2 lb baking potatoes, peeled and quartered

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the potatoes (and garlic, if using), turn the heat to medium and simmer about 15 minutes, until easily pierced with a fork.
When the potatoes are nearly done, warm the milk and butter in a small saucepan over low heat until the butter melts.
Drain well and return the potatoes to the hot pot for 1–2 minutes to steam off excess moisture.
Mash, adding the warm milk gradually until smooth and creamy (you may not need it all). Season, and top with extra butter if you like.

tips: Stir in up to 1 cup shredded Cheddar or Parmesan, or top with crispy fried onions or crumbled bacon.
They can be made up to 2 days ahead. Reheat with a splash of milk and a little butter.

ingredients.title: Eggplant
items: ¼ cup olive oil, for frying

ingredients.title: Breadcrumbs
items: 6 slices bread, or 1½ cups store-bought breadcrumbs

ingredients.title: Toppings
items: 1½ cups marinara (up to 2½ cups if you like it saucy)

steps.text: Trim the eggplants and slice them into ¼–½-inch rounds.
**Breadcrumbs:** Toast the bread and pulse it into crumbs in a food processor. Mix with the Parmesan, Italian herbs, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow bowls: flour, beaten eggs and the crumbs. Stir a pinch of salt into the flour and the eggs.
Coat each slice in flour, then egg, then press it into the crumbs.
Cook the slices by one of these methods:
sub: **Pan-fry:** 2–3 minutes per side in 1–2 tbsp oil at a time, until golden. Drain on paper towels.
**Bake (less oil):** arrange on a sheet pan brushed with 1–2 tbsp oil and bake at 350°F (175°C) for about 25 minutes, until golden.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spread a generous layer of marinara over the bottom of a large baking dish.
Layer the eggplant, mozzarella, a few spoonfuls of marinara and some Parmesan, then repeat once more.
Bake uncovered 30 minutes, until bubbling and browned. Scatter with basil and oregano and serve.

items.title: Gamja Salad (Korean Potato Salad)

items: 1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch pieces
¼ tsp ground white pepper (or black)

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with ¼ tsp salt and let it sit 5 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites and chop the whites. Press 1 yolk through a sieve to use as a garnish; keep the other 2.
Rinse the potatoes in cold water to remove excess starch. Put them in a heavy pot with ½ cup water and a pinch of salt and cook over medium-high heat for 20 minutes.
Drain off any water, return the potatoes to the pot, cover and leave over very low heat for 1–2 minutes to dry out.
Mash the hot potatoes for 30 seconds, then mash in the 2 reserved yolks and the chopped whites.
Mix in the cucumber, pepper and rice syrup, then the mayonnaise. Let it cool, then refrigerate. Serve cold, garnished with the sieved yolk.

tips: Makes a great sandwich: a scoop on lettuce between slices of toasted bread.

items.title: Garlic Mashed Potatoes

items: 1 tbsp salt, for the cooking water

steps.text: Put the potatoes, garlic and 1 tbsp salt in a saucepan with water to cover by 1 inch. Bring to a boil over high heat, then simmer over medium-low 10–12 minutes, until fork-tender.
Drain, return the potatoes to the hot pan and stir about 1 minute to dry them out.
Stir in the butter a piece at a time, letting each melt before adding more.
Mash in the milk until smooth, then stir in the kosher salt and white pepper. Top with extra butter if you like.

tips: Adding the butter before the milk keeps them creamier for longer with less liquid, and cooking the garlic with the potatoes mellows it.
Russets work but are starchier and less creamy. A spoonful of sour cream and some chives are good additions.
**Roasted garlic version:** Cut the top off a whole bulb, drizzle with olive oil, wrap in foil and roast at 400°F (200°C) for about 40 minutes. Squeeze the soft cloves into the potatoes and mash.

items.title: Italian Sausage Stuffed Zucchini
items.note: Zucchini boats filled with seared chicken sausage, Italian breadcrumbs, basil and two cheeses. Hearty enough to be dinner.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Score the flesh of each zucchini half in a crosshatch, as you would to dice an avocado, and scoop it out into a large bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sausage and cook until seared, about 6 minutes.
Transfer the sausage to the large bowl and add the breadcrumbs, ½ cup of the mozzarella, the fontina, garlic and basil. Mix well.
Spoon the filling into the zucchini shells and top with the remaining ¼ cup mozzarella.
Bake until the zucchini is tender and the cheese is golden, about 15 minutes.

source.name: Guga Foods on YouTube (recipe from Nate From The Internet)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and generously butter a baking dish.
In a large bowl, toss the potatoes with salt, pepper, the rosemary and thyme, and most of the Gruyère and Parmesan (save a handful for the top).
Spread the potatoes in the dish and pour the cream over them.
Bake for 2 hours.
Scatter the reserved cheese over the top and slide it under the broiler until browned and crusty.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

items: 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a baking sheet.
Bake the squash skin-side down about 1 hour, until cooked through. Cool 10 minutes, then scrape the flesh into strands with a fork.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion until it starts to turn translucent. Stir in the mushrooms and kale and turn the heat to medium-low.
Add the squash, the remaining 2 tbsp butter, the garlic salt, Italian seasoning and red pepper flakes and cook 2 minutes.
Transfer to a large bowl and stir in the pesto and olive oil, then the Parmesan.

items.title: Traditional Sweet Potato Casserole
items.note: The holiday standby: mashed sweet potatoes with brown sugar and vanilla, finished with pecans and toasted marshmallows.

items: 2½ lb sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
½ cup finely chopped pecans, divided

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Put the sweet potatoes in a Dutch oven and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and let cool slightly.
Transfer the potatoes to a large bowl, add the brown sugar, butter, salt and vanilla, and mash with a potato masher until smooth. Fold in ¼ cup of the pecans.
Spread the mixture evenly in an 11 × 7-inch baking dish coated with cooking spray. Sprinkle with the remaining ¼ cup pecans and top with the marshmallows.
Bake until golden, about 25 minutes.

tips: Rather have a crunchy brown-sugar and pecan crumble than marshmallows? See the Yummy Sweet Potato Casserole.

items.title: Yummy Sweet Potato Casserole

steps.text: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Cover the sweet potatoes with water in a saucepan and cook over medium-high heat 10–15 minutes, until fork-tender. Drain and put them in a large bowl.
Mash with a fork, then mix in the eggs. Add the sugar, milk, butter, vanilla and salt and mix until smooth. Spread in a 9 × 13 baking dish.
**Topping:** Mix the brown sugar and flour, then cut in the butter with a pastry cutter until it looks like coarse crumbs. Stir in the pecans and sprinkle over the sweet potatoes.
Bake about 30 minutes, until the topping is lightly browned.

tips: An immersion blender makes the filling extra creamy.
Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and keep the topping separate in the fridge. Add the topping just before baking, and allow a few extra minutes if the dish is cold.
Leftovers keep 3–4 days. Reheat covered at 350°F for 20–25 minutes.

chapters.title: Breads & Baking
chapters.blurb: Naan, pretzel rolls, two pizza crusts and two loaves, then pound cake, pecan pie, brownies, bread pudding and more.

items.title: Jay's Signature Pizza Crust
items.time: Prep 30 min, plus 1 hr rising · Bake 15–20 min

steps.text: Stir the warm water, yeast and brown sugar together in a large bowl and leave 10 minutes.

Stir in the oil and salt, then mix in 2½ cups of the flour. Turn out onto a floured surface and knead, working in the remaining flour a little at a time, until the dough is no longer sticky. Put it in an oiled bowl.
Cover with a towel and let rise about 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch the dough down, shape it into a tight ball and let it relax 1 minute before rolling out.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
On a pizza stone, add toppings and bake right away. On a pan, oil the pan and let the dough rise 15–20 minutes before topping.
Bake 15–20 minutes, until the cheese melts and the crust is golden.

items.title: Naan
items.time: Prep 30 min · Rise 1 hr · Cook 10 min

items: 1 packet (¼ oz / 2¼ tsp) active dry yeast
1 tbsp oil, plus more for the pan

steps.text: Stir the sugar, warm water and yeast together and leave about 10 minutes, until foamy.
Heap the flour on a work surface (start with 300 g) and make a well in the middle. Add the yeast mixture, yogurt, salt and 1 tbsp oil and knead about 10 minutes, until smooth and shiny.
Cover with a damp cloth and leave in a warm place about 1 hour, until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces and roll each into a 6-inch round.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat and lightly oil it. Cook one naan at a time until it puffs and the underside has browned blisters, then flip and cook the other side.
Brush with melted butter or ghee, sprinkle with cilantro and serve warm.

tips: Flour absorbs differently depending on the weather. Add flour beyond 300 g only if the dough is still sticky.
The pan needs to be very hot to get those blisters.

items.title: No-Knead Soft Pretzel Rolls
items.time: 8–10 hr rise + 4–5 hr proof · Bake 25 min

ingredients.title: Dough
items: 13 g kosher salt (4 tsp Diamond Crystal, or 2 tsp Morton or fine sea salt)
14 g (1 tbsp) olive oil or neutral oil

steps.text: Whisk the flour, yeast, salt and sugar in a large bowl. Add the water and oil and stir into a shaggy, sticky dough, kneading briefly in the bowl until it comes together.
Cover airtight and let rise until doubled, 8–10 hours.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and divide into 10 pieces (about 112 g each).
Shape each into a tight ball: pull the edges into the center, flip it seam-down, then drag it toward you with cupped hands to tighten the surface.
Space the balls in a floured container or two 9 × 13 pans, cover and proof 4–5 hours, until doubled and very airy.
Heat the oven to 400°F (204°C) and line two sheet pans with parchment.
Bring the 8 cups of water to a simmer, lower the heat and stir in the baking soda. Keep it barely simmering.

One at a time, lower a ball into the water top-side down, flip it over and back again, then lift it out with a spider. The whole dip should take no more than 30 seconds. Set it top-side up on a pan, five to a pan.
Brush with butter, sprinkle generously with flaky salt and slash the tops twice with a razor or sharp knife. Bake 22–25 minutes, until deep brown.
Brush with more butter straight out of the oven. Repeat with the second pan. Cool briefly, or completely if using for sandwiches.

tips: A kitchen scale makes this much more reliable.
Active dry yeast: sprinkle it over the cold water and let it stand 15 minutes before mixing.
Faster version (not tested by the author): use 2 tsp instant yeast and lukewarm water, rise 2–3 hours, then proof the shaped rolls at least 1 hour.
After the first rise the dough can wait in the fridge; let shaped rolls proof at room temperature until very light before boiling.

items.title: Quick and Easy Pizza Crust
items.time: Prep 10 min, plus 15 min standing · Bake 15–20 min

items: Sauce and toppings of your choice

steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and lightly grease a pizza pan.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and leave about 10 minutes, until creamy.
